ass:iid.detail: The paper’s iid assertion is equivalent to the sample law being the product of n copies of the observed-data law, as defined by IidSample.

ass:randomized-independence.detail: The paper’s joint independence assertion is exactly the finite-atom probability factorization required by RandomizedIndependence.

ass:balanced-randomization.detail: The paper’s treatment probability equals the armMass P true equality defining BalancedRandomization.

ass:consistency.detail: The stated equality of realized and treatment-selected potential measurements is equivalent, as an almost-sure random-variable equality, to Consistency assigning zero probability to every violating atom.

ass:mar.detail: The stated conditional independence is equivalent to MissingAtRandom’s cross-multiplied factorization on positive-probability cells, with null cells imposing no additional restriction.

lem:identification-infrastructure.detail: The paper matches the Lean theorem’s finite binary model, five law-class assumptions, floor range q∈[1/2,1], observation map, ATE identification identity, and zero contribution from null cells.

lem:upper-risk.detail: UpperRiskCertificate asserts exactly a positive universal constant bounding the estimator’s squared risk for all stated parameters, legal laws, and iid observed samples.

lem:honest-interval-construction.detail: The hypotheses and all coverage, pointwise length, expected length, and radius-dependent conclusions match the six conjuncts of honest_interval_construction.

def:rate.detail: Expanding gScale gives the displayed rate because the dimension ratio is nonnegative on the meaningful parameter range.

prop:complete-arrival-reduction.detail: All quantifiers, Cartesian-sample identities, projection inequalities, risk bounds, and uniform minimax comparisons match complete_arrival_reduction and its mapped definitions.

thm:interval-frontier.detail: The paper matches the Lean parameter ranges, constants depending only on α, and uniform two-sided square-root rate bounds for minimax expected interval length; finiteness follows from the constants being real numbers.
